title: Tech Stocks Power S&P 500 Rally
text:
Strong: Information Technology, Financials, Energy, Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary Weak: Real Estate, Consumer Staples, Utilities, Health Care Moving the Market
Facebook 's (FB) "good enough" earnings report tempers stock negativity; price action fuels tech-rally
High-growth tech stocks outperform the broader market
Buying efforts concentrated in the cyclical sectors; defensive-oriented sectors underperform
Expectation that fund managers need to boost portfolio equity weightings following the October sell-off Tech Stocks Power S&P 500 Rally 31-Oct-18 13:00 ET Dow +326.98 at 25201.62, Nasdaq +171.18 at 7333.02, S&P +42.26 at 2725.03
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 has extended yesterday's rally, currently up 1.5%, propelled by a resurgence in large-cap technology stocks, which are up after Facebook (FB 151.70, +5.49, +3.7%) released its third quarter results last evening. The tech-sensitive Nasdaq Composite outperforms the broader market, up 2.2%. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 1.3%, while the Russell 2000 underperforms, just up 0.7%.
Facebook's"good enough" earnings report has tempered negativity surrounding the stock, and its positive price action has spread to the other FANG names. Facebook reported above-consensus earnings and increased its revenue growth outlook, easing nerves after the social network warned of growth-deceleration last quarter.
The FANG bunch has subsequently fed the information technology (+2.6%), communication services (+2.2%), and consumer discretionary (+1.9%) sectors with healthy gains. Apple (AAPL 219.32, +6.01, +2.7%) leads the S&P's most heavily-weighted tech sector higher, while Amazon (AMZN 1594.29, +66.08, +4.2%) reverses its recent struggles to lift the consumer discretionary sector. Likewise, Netflix (NFLX 305.95, +19.14, +6.7%) and Alphabet (GOOG 1078.00, +41.79, +4.0%) join Facebook to fuel the communication sector.
Another strong sector has been the financials group, which is up with bond yields today, adding 2.0%. Top-weighted JPMorgan Chase (JPM 109.03, +2.32) and Bank of America (BAC 27.56, +0.78) provide strong support with respective gains of 2.2% and 3.0%. Meanwhile, the yield on the benchmark 10-yr Treasury note is up four basis points at 3.14%.
Conversely, the defensive-oriented real estate (-0.4%), consumer staples (-0.8%), and utilities (-0.8%) sectors are the only groups in negative territory today.
Also contributing to today's rally has been month-end activity from fund managers and possibly some short-term covering activity. There is an underlying expectation for fund managers to boost their portfolio equity weightings following this month's sell-off. Concurrently, it stands to reason that short-term sellers are covering their positions, as the market enters what is historically a favorable seasonal period.
Overseas, equities finished Wednesday on a higher note, closing the door on a bruising October. Japan's Nikkei gained 2.1% after the Bank of Japan made no changes to its policy stance, and China's Shanghai Composite (+1.4%) added another consecutive gain. Meanwhile, France's CAC led the major European indices higher with a gain of 2.3%.
Reviewing today's economic data: The third quarter employment cost index increased 0.8% (Briefing.com consensus +0.7) versus 0.6% in the second quarter. Wages and salaries, which comprise about 70% of compensation costs, increased 0.9%, while benefit costs jumped 0.4%. The key takeaway from the report is that it corroborates a trend of rising compensation costs for civilian workers that have been discussed by employers and which have kept the Federal Reserve on a tightening path. The ADP National Employment Report showed an increase of 227,000 in October (Briefing.com consensus 180,000), and the September reading was revised to 218,000 (from 230,000).
